title: Primary Care Provider Assignment: Carry-Over of Unexpired Specialist Referrals
content:
**Desk system reference — Primary Care Provider Assignment, carried specialist referrals.**

## Policy

A single referral that one of the member's earlier primary care assignments issued, and that is still within its validity, is carried onto the member's current active assignment under its original referral number and its original issue date, so that it keeps its own expiry, and the carried entry records the visits the referral still covers.

Carrying a referral changes where the referral is listed, not when it runs out: the expiry still follows from the original issue date. The carried entry appears in the current assignment's referral history as a single referral to the specialist named on the earlier referral.

| Point | Position |
|---|---|
| Referral that can be carried | A single referral issued under an earlier Primary Care Provider Assignment of the member, still within its validity |
| Assignment it is carried onto | The member's current active assignment |
| Referral number on the carried entry | The original referral number, unchanged |
| Issue date on the carried entry | The original issue date, so the referral keeps its own expiry |
| What the carried entry records | The visits the referral still covers |

## System entry: `carry_over_referral_de0684af`

**Capability.** Carries an unexpired specialist referral that a member's earlier primary care provider issued onto the member's current primary care assignment. One call adds one referral entry to the current assignment's referral history, under the referral's original number and original issue date, as a single-type referral to the named specialist covering the number of visits given. Nothing else on the member's record changes; the member and the specialist's office see the referral listed under the current primary care provider.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the representative unlocks `carry_over_referral_de0684af` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `pcp_assignment_id` | Reference number of the member's current primary care assignment the referral is carried onto | As it appears on the member's primary care assignment record |
| `referral_number` | Referral number of the earlier referral being carried | Copied character for character from the earlier assignment's referral entry, with no change to letters, digits or hyphens |
| `specialist_npi` | NPI of the specialist named on the earlier referral | 10-digit NPI, digits only, no spaces or punctuation |
| `issue_date` | Original issue date of the earlier referral | Calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format, exactly as on the earlier entry |
| `referral_visits` | Number of specialist visits the carried referral covers on the current assignment | Whole non-negative number of visits, no decimals |

**Return.** A receipt with: `status` (the text "carried" when the entry was recorded), `pcp_event_id` (reference of the new referral history entry), `pcp_assignment_id` (the current assignment the referral now sits on), `referral_number` (the carried referral number), `specialist_npi` (10-digit NPI), `issue_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the original issue date kept on the entry) and `referral_visits` (integer visits recorded). A receipt with status "carried" means the referral is now listed on the current assignment.

**Illustration (hypothetical values).** Called with an assignment reference, referral number RF-2603-41127, NPI 1234567893, issue date 2026-03-04 and 5 visits, the receipt returns status "carried" with the same referral number, NPI, issue date 2026-03-04 and 5 visits, and a new entry reference.
